questions.subject: ENT
questions.topic: Larynx: hoarseness, stridor, vocal cord palsy, tracheostomy
questions.stem: A 4-year-old develops a barking cough, inspiratory stridor and hoarseness over two days with low-grade fever and no drooling. What is the diagnosis and the key treatment?
options: Epiglottitis, treated with urgent intubation
Bacterial tracheitis, treated with antistaphylococcal antibiotics
Acute laryngotracheobronchitis, treated with nebulised adrenaline and systemic corticosteroid
Retropharyngeal abscess, treated by drainage
questions.concept: Croup is viral, usually parainfluenza, and the gradual onset with a barking cough and preserved swallowing distinguishes it from epiglottitis, where a toxic child sits forward drooling with a muffled voice and no cough.
questions.reference: Dhingra Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat 8e, Ch. Diseases of Larynx

questions.subject: ENT
questions.topic: Nasal polyps, granulomatous disease & tumours of nose and PNS
questions.stem: A young man from a rural area has a friable strawberry-like polypoidal mass in the nose that bleeds on touch, with white dots on its surface. Which organism is responsible?
options: Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis
Rhinosporidium seeberi, acquired from stagnant pond water
Aspergillus fumigatus
Mycobacterium leprae
questions.concept: The white dots are sporangia packed with spores, treatment is wide surgical excision with cautery of the base because recurrence is common, and dapsone is used as an adjunct.
questions.reference: Dhingra Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat 8e, Ch. Diseases of Nose and Paranasal Sinuses

questions.subject: ENT
questions.topic: Neck spaces, deep neck infection & aerodigestive foreign bodies
questions.stem: A 6-year-old has a painless midline neck swelling that moves upward on protrusion of the tongue. What is the diagnosis and the correct operation?
options: Branchial cyst, excised alone
Dermoid cyst, excised alone
Thyroglossal cyst, requiring Sistrunk operation with excision of the central hyoid body
Cystic hygroma, treated with sclerotherapy
questions.concept: The tract follows the descent of the thyroid from the foramen caecum, so leaving the hyoid segment or the tract to the tongue base behind is the usual cause of recurrence.
questions.reference: Dhingra Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat 8e, Ch. Neck Masses

questions.subject: ENT
questions.topic: Oral cavity, salivary gland & pharyngeal disease
questions.stem: An elderly woman has dysphagia, regurgitation of undigested food, halitosis and a gurgling swelling in the left neck. Which condition is this and where does it arise?
options: A pharyngeal pouch herniating through Killian dehiscence between the two parts of the inferior constrictor
An oesophageal diverticulum at the carina
A branchial cyst of the second arch
A laryngocele through the thyrohyoid membrane
questions.concept: Cricopharyngeal dysfunction raises pressure above the sphincter, blind nasogastric or endoscopic instrumentation risks perforating the pouch, and treatment is endoscopic stapled diverticulotomy or open excision with myotomy.
questions.reference: Dhingra Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat 8e, Ch. Diseases of Oral Cavity and Pharynx

questions.subject: ENT
questions.stem: A child born with profound bilateral sensorineural deafness has received no benefit from hearing aids at 18 months. Which intervention offers the best speech outcome and why is timing critical?
options: A bone-anchored hearing aid, timing being unimportant
Cochlear implantation, because auditory cortical plasticity declines sharply after the first few years
Repeat hearing aid trial until school age
Middle ear implant after the age of 6
questions.concept: The implant bypasses non-functioning hair cells to stimulate the cochlear nerve directly, and implantation within the sensitive period gives far better spoken language than late surgery, which is the rationale for newborn screening.
questions.reference: Dhingra Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat 8e, Ch. Hearing Loss and Rehabilitation

questions.subject: ENT
questions.stem: A 30-year-old has long-standing bilateral nasal obstruction and uses a topical decongestant several times daily; the mucosa is boggy and obstruction is now worse than before. What has happened?
options: Atrophic rhinitis has developed
Allergic rhinitis has progressed
Rhinitis medicamentosa from rebound vasodilatation after prolonged topical decongestant use
A nasal polyp has formed
questions.concept: Tachyphylaxis and rebound congestion follow use beyond about 5 to 7 days, and management is withdrawal of the decongestant under cover of an intranasal corticosteroid with saline irrigation.
questions.reference: Dhingra Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat 8e, Ch. Diseases of Nose and Sinuses

questions.subject: ENT
questions.stem: A teenager has fever, membranous tonsillitis, marked cervical lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly, with atypical lymphocytes on the blood film. Which drug should be avoided and why?
options: Paracetamol, because of hepatotoxicity
Penicillin, because of anaphylaxis risk
Ampicillin or amoxicillin, because a florid maculopapular rash follows in infectious mononucleosis
Corticosteroid, because it worsens the infection
questions.concept: The illness is Epstein-Barr virus infection confirmed by a positive Paul-Bunnell or monospot test, treatment is supportive, and contact sport is avoided for weeks because of the risk of splenic rupture.
questions.reference: Dhingra Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat 8e, Ch. Diseases of Oropharynx

questions.subject: ENT
questions.topic: Vertigo, Meniere's disease & facial nerve palsy
questions.stem: A man develops brief vertigo and a sensorineural hearing loss immediately after lifting a heavy weight, with a positive fistula test and no history of ear disease. What is the likely diagnosis?
options: A perilymph fistula at the oval or round window from a sudden pressure change
Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo
Vestibular neuritis
Meniere disease
questions.concept: Barotrauma or straining can rupture the window membranes, so bed rest with head elevation and avoidance of straining is tried first and exploratory tympanotomy with graft repair follows if the loss progresses.
questions.reference: Dhingra Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat 8e, Ch. Vertigo
